industries.education.name: Education
industries.education.lead: Educational institutions have two different reasons to use robots. The building: hallways need cleaning every day, ideally while lessons are on. The lab: universities and colleges need humanoids and platforms for students to learn on.
industries.education.lead2: These tasks have different buyers and budgets, so this page has two entry points.

industries.education.heads.problems: Why school buildings are hard to clean.
industries.education.problems.items.0.te: Sanitary rules for educational institutions require daily wet cleaning of all rooms.
industries.education.problems.items.1.ti: Class time is the only slot
industries.education.problems.items.1.te: Hallways get dirty at breaks, and mopping among children is awkward. That leaves class time, when everyone is in class.
industries.education.problems.items.2.te: Over 80% of cleaning staff are foreign nationals, and regions are tightening migrant hiring rules.
industries.education.problems.items.3.te: Cleaning companies’ payroll has grown two- to threefold in five years, and that goes into the price of cleaning contracts.

industries.education.directions.lead: The facilities service buys building cleaning; a department or the university’s development program buys the lab. So we price them separately.
Cleaning hallways and corridors during lessons
A robotic scrubber cleans hallways while children are in class, then returns to its station by itself. The station charges it, drains dirty water and refills clean.
A separate scheduled cycle: the gym when no class is using it, the cafeteria after the lunch rush.
Humanoids, quadrupeds and mobile platforms for university departments and colleges: we put together a set for your curriculum and budget, then deliver and launch it.
Buyer: a school, an education department or campus facilities.

industries.education.economy.title: Buying takes years to pay back. We say so.
industries.education.economy.lead: The robot takes over part of a cleaner’s shift, not the whole of it. So if a school buys one, payback takes years, not months.
industries.education.economy.shiftLabel: A cleaner’s eight-hour shift: the robot covers 2.5 hours out of 8, which is 31 percent

industries.education.economy.ways.title: What this means
industries.education.economy.ways.rent.t: Rental or cleaning as a service
No capital spending and no five-year wait. Robotic cleaning can be bought as a service, just as schools already buy cleaning services under Federal Law No. 44-FZ.
The robot washes the long hallways; people do what it can’t: classrooms, restrooms, stairs. At School No. 281 the cleaners stayed and now handle the classrooms.
